question: Examine the continuity of $g(x)=x-[x]$ at $x=2$, where $[x]$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $x$. Give mathematical justification.
explanation:
Function value at $x=2$
$$g(2)=2-[2]=0$$
Left-hand limit
For $x\to 2^-$, $[x]=1$. Hence, $$\lim_{x\to 2^-}g(x)=\lim_{x\to 2^-}(x-1)=1$$
Right-hand limit
For $x\to 2^+$, $[x]=2$. Hence, $$\lim_{x\to 2^+}g(x)=\lim_{x\to 2^+}(x-2)=0$$
Comparison of one-sided limits
Since $$\lim_{x\to 2^-}g(x)\neq \lim_{x\to 2^+}g(x),$$ the limit of $g(x)$ at $x=2$ does not exist.
Therefore, $g$ is discontinuous at $x=2$.

options.A: $g$ is continuous at $x=2$ because both one-sided limits are $0$.
options.C: $g$ is discontinuous at $x=2$ because both one-sided limits equal $1$.
options.D: $g$ is discontinuous at $x=2$ because the left-hand limit is $1$ and the right-hand limit is $0$.
